header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Jordan Lee (AE), Priya Nair (SE), Liam Chen (SA)
Attendees (Belleview): Michael Ortiz (CISO), Sara Patel (Head of IT), Aisha Khan (Compliance), Tom Rivers (Cloud Eng), Emily Zhao (Security Analyst)
summary: Redwood walked Belleview through SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture, trust center access, controls mapping approach, RBAC/SSO integration options, audit log retention and encryption/KMS choices. Customer expressed interest in hosted API with VPC/private deployment options and needs evidence for ISO Annex A mapping. Agreed next steps to share reports, mapping spreadsheet, and schedule a technical deep dive.
topics: Trust Center access and evidence download
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for isolation
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, we're gonna do a quick SOC 2 / ISO posture runthrough. Priya is here from the SE team. Michael: yep thanks Jordan, we got a handful of folks on the call.
[00:18] Michael Ortiz: Quick context, we're in the middle of an ISO 27001 readiness push and also preparing for a SOC 2 renewal. main asks are: how we can map Redwood controls to our internal control IDs, and what evidence we can pull for auditors.
[00:36] Priya Nair: Great, thanks Michael. So high level, Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering security and availability, and we also provide a Trust Center where customers can download evidence artifacts, control narratives, and a controls mapping template.
[00:50] Sara Patel: Is the Trust Center access time-limited? our procurement expects that we can share artifacts with third party auditors.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Yes you can grant auditor access, there's an auditor role for one-time access or temporary credentials, and we log all artifact downloads. small note, sometimes the auto transcript says "Trust Center" as "Trust Center" fine but internal doc names might differ.
[01:25] Aisha Khan: Do you provide ISO mapping out of the box? like Annex A controls?
[01:35] Priya Nair: We provide a mapping between Redwood controls and common frameworks (SOC 2 criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A, NIST CSF). It's a spreadsheet — we'll send the initial template and example evidence items.
[01:50] Tom Rivers: From a cloud eng perspective we need to know KMS options. can customers bring their own KMS or use Redwood-managed? and where are keys stored (region)?
[02:08] Liam Chen: Short answer: both options. We support Redwood-managed envelope encryption and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations with major cloud providers. Key residency follows the region you select for your private deployment — if you choose a dedicated or private VPC in eu-west-1 the KMS is in that region.
[02:26] Emily Zhao: How about logging — do you push audit logs to our splunk or we have to pull from your console? retention?
[02:40] Priya Nair: We have streaming integrations for audit logs — you can stream to your SIEM (SPLUNK, Sumologic, Datadog) or opt to pull zips from the Trust Center. Retention is configurable; default is 90 days in the console but for enterprise we can do longer retention via dedicated buckets and custom retention policies.
[03:00] Michael Ortiz: For ISO we need proof of RBAC enforcement and SSO details. how are roles mapped and do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning?
[03:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, SAML SSO is supported along with SCIM for user provisioning. Roles are RBAC-based, you can map IdP groups to specific Redwood roles. We'll share docs that show the role matrix and an example SAML assertion.
[03:33] Sara Patel: Are there any controls that are not covered because of hosted multi-tenant architecture?
[03:42] Priya Nair: There are a few controls that customers sometimes want stronger isolation for — e.g., physical separation and some data residency guarantees. For that we offer Dedicated and Private deployment options with isolated GPU pools and VPC peering. For SOC 2 the Type II report describes our segmentation controls and controls around logical separation.
[04:05] Michael Ortiz: auditors will ask for evidence of change control and patching cadence, do you have runbooks we can share?
[04:15] Liam Chen: We have patching windows, automated deployments, and change control logs. We can provide sanitized runbooks and evidence snapshots — timeline of deployments and config changes mapped to tickets.
[04:30] Aisha Khan: about encryption in transit — TLS up to the edge?
[04:36] Priya Nair: All traffic is TLS 1.2+; internal service-to-service communication is mTLS in dedicated/private modes. For hosted API, we terminate at the edge but you can enable private networking for extra controls.
[04:50] Tom Rivers: Data residency: can you pin data to a region? If we select EU region, does any tenant metadata leave region?
[05:02] Jordan Lee: For Private deployments and Dedicated customers we can guarantee residency. For hosted multi-tenant there are region controls for processing but some metadata like billing receipts may be in the US by default — we can discuss contractual addenda for stricter residency.
[05:22] Emily Zhao: On audit logs, can we get raw request headers or only aggregated events?
[05:30] Priya Nair: You can get request-level logs with headers redacted by default; for sensitive header capture you need an elevated agreement. We'll note that and include the logging schema when we send artifacts.
[05:50] Michael Ortiz: Ok let's talk about evidence for SOC 2: sample of control tests, vulnerability scan results, penetration test reports — do you share the full pen test or a sanitized executive summary?
[06:05] Jordan Lee: We generally provide an executive summary of third-party pentest reports and more detailed findings in the Trust Center for redacted items. SOC 2 includes a description of our monitoring and vulnerability mgmt program. Full raw pentest artifacts are not usually shared but we can provide the report and remediation timeline.
[06:25] Sara Patel: For ISO Annex A mapping, do you include control owners and evidence references?
[06:33] Priya Nair: The mapping template includes our control ID, applicable framework control (e.g., A.12.4.1 — event logging), the evidence artifact name in the Trust Center and suggested customer evidence to collect. We'll ask you to map to your internal control IDs in that sheet.
[06:50] Aisha Khan: How quickly can you provide artifact timestamps? auditors often want timestamps showing when logs were collected — is that included?
[07:00] Liam Chen: Yes each artifact download and log stream includes timestamps. The Trust Center artifact metadata includes creation and collection timestamps and checksum.
[07:18] Michael Ortiz: Can you support an auditor performing read-only queries against a sandbox environment for a week? we've done that before with other vendors.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: We can facilitate auditor access in a sandbox/dedicated environment for a limited window. We'll need a formal request and an NDA signed by the auditor, but that's in scope.
[07:45] Tom Rivers: On the KMS integration, if we bring our own keys, do you do client-side encryption or server-side encryption with customer-managed keys?
[07:55] Liam Chen: We do server-side encryption with customer-managed KMS; data is encrypted at rest with envelope keys and the master keys reside in your KMS. For extremely sensitive use cases we can discuss client-side encryption patterns too.
[08:10] Emily Zhao: What's the cadence of SOC 2 renewals? we need the timeframe to schedule our internal audit.
[08:18] Jordan Lee: SOC 2 is annual; our latest Type II period covered Jan–Dec 2024 and report issued Q1 2025. We'll share the report and cover letter which states the period.
[08:32] Michael Ortiz: If we go private deployment, what's the onboarding timeline?
[08:40] Priya Nair: Private deployments typically take 6–8 weeks after contract signature for standard configs; if you need custom networking or KMS integration it can be 8–12 weeks. We'll put together a project plan once we get confirmation.
[09:00] Sara Patel: Any SLA differences between hosted and dedicated?
[09:06] Jordan Lee: Yes Dedicated includes response-time SLAs and guaranteed capacity. Hosted has best-effort latency SLOs and usage-based pricing. We'll include the SLA doc in the follow-up.
[09:20] Aisha Khan: Does Redwood maintain ISO 27001 certification?
[09:25] Priya Nair: Redwood itself is not fully ISO 27001 certified as a company right now, but we maintain a controls mapping against Annex A and we actively support customers' ISO audits with mapped evidence. We're on the roadmap for certification and can provide interim evidence.
[09:45] Michael Ortiz: For our risk register, we need to understand residual risk from multi-tenant hosting; can you provide a risk statement and mitigating controls?
[09:58] Liam Chen: Yes, we'll provide a risk summary document that outlines threats, likelihood, and compensating controls — e.g., logical separation, encryption, access controls, monitoring and incident response.
[10:12] Jordan Lee: Quick note — sometimes the transcription will show "KV cache" as "K V cache" etc; ignore minor transcription artifacts in the transcript.
[10:22] Tom Rivers: Any limitations on export formats from the Trust Center? csv, pdf, json?
[10:30] Priya Nair: Trust Center supports PDF for reports, CSV/Excel exports for logs and mapping spreadsheets, and JSON for API-driven artifacts. We'll include sample exports.
[10:45] Emily Zhao: Will you share the logging schema and field descriptions?
[10:50] Priya Nair: Yes, that will be part of the artifact bundle.
[11:05] Michael Ortiz: On SSO provisioning, can you support both Okta and Azure AD?
[11:10] Jordan Lee: Yes both, and we support group mapping via SCIM for Azure AD and Okta. We'll attach SAML metadata and a SCIM example.
[11:25] Sara Patel: For auditors, can we get contact for someone on Redwood side who can respond to questions during audit window?
[11:32] Jordan Lee: Yes Jordan and Priya will be primary contacts; we'll include an escalation list for on-call engineers if needed.
[11:45] Aisha Khan: About evidence retention: if you purge artifacts after 90 days, will the Trust Center still have historical artifacts for auditors?
[11:55] Priya Nair: For enterprise customers we retain evidence for custom retention windows; we'll set an archival bucket for your account for the audit period if needed.
[12:10] Michael Ortiz: Ok let's recap and next steps.
[12:15] Jordan Lee: Recap — we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report, Trust Center access and auditor flow, controls mapping template, sample evidence artifacts and logging schema. We'll coordinate timing for a technical deep dive with Tom and Emily to verify KMS and SIEM integrations.
[12:37] Tom Rivers: Sounds good. we'll review internally and get back about preferred deployment (hosted vs private) and KMS ownership.
[12:45] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifact bundle within 3 business days.
[12:52] Michael Ortiz: Thanks — appreciate it.
[12:55] [call ended]
